Booked a Hakone room "with private open-air bath"? At one Gora ryokan we checked, that room cost ¥12,600 more for two, and the plan page admits the bath isn't hot-spring water. Here's how to get the real thing 👇

🤔 Guess first: which of these three gets you real onsen water for the least money? 👉 https://japanbystation.com/hakone-private-onsen-which-booking

We went through the small print on the booking pages line by line before writing this, because the word "private" covers three very different evenings in Hakone.

♨️ THE THREE OPTIONS

1️⃣ In-room bath. On Wednesday 16 December 2026, Kiritani Hakoneso in Gora listed its standard two-meal plan at ¥27,000 for two on Ikyu, and its room with an open-air bath at ¥39,600. The catch is written right there: the in-room baths are not onsen water.

2️⃣ The inn's private bath. The same ryokan's private open-air bath uses its milky sulphur water: ¥3,600 for 50 minutes for two, five groups a day, slots given out in check-in order.

3️⃣ A day-use private bath. Hakone Yuryo, a 3-minute free shuttle from Hakone-Yumoto Station, has 19 private open-air bath rooms. The smallest are ¥10,400 for two hours on weekdays, booked online with a guaranteed time.

💭 OUR TAKE

For most couples, a standard room plus the inn's private bath is the sweet spot, as long as you check in early. Arriving late? Book the two-hour private room in Yumoto instead and stop worrying about slots.

There's something quietly lovely about a hot-spring bath that's just yours for an hour, steam rising, nobody waiting at the door. It's worth getting the booking right.
